title: Granularity- and Interference-Aware GPU Sharing with MPS
problem: Naively co-scheduling multiple HPC and DNN workloads on shared GPUs leads to performance degradation due to resource contention. Existing CUDA MPS mechanisms do not account for interference patterns when combining workflows.
motivation: GPU acceleration is essential for exascale HPC performance, but most applications under-utilize available GPU resources, requiring efficient resource sharing to improve utilization, throughput, and energy efficiency.
method: The approach profiles HPC and DNN workloads to characterize resource requirements and interference patterns. It optimizes scheduling configurations using profiling data to right-size GPU resources for specific workflow combinations, then collocates workflows using CUDA MPS while considering granularity and interference patterns to maximize throughput and energy efficiency metrics.
key_novelty: Granularity- and interference-aware scheduling that uses workload profiling to guide optimal workflow colocation decisions on shared GPUs.
contributions: Scheduling approach that optimizes workflow configurations to maximize throughput and energy efficiency metrics
Workload profiling-based method for right-sizing GPU resources in multi-workflow scenarios
Demonstrates 2x throughput and 1.6x energy efficiency improvements using CUDA MPS on NVIDIA A100X GPUs
